value.text: Our strategy is to deliver insights and experiences essential to investing, with a keen focus on innovation across data, research, product, and delivery

strategic_priorities.quote: Our strategy is to deliver insights and experiences essential to investing. Proprietary data sets, meaningful analytics, independent research, and effective investment strategies are at the core of the powerful digital solutions that investors across our client segments rely on. We have a keen focus on innovation across data, research, product, and delivery so that we can effectively cater to the evolving needs and expectations of investors globally.

value.text: Deliver differentiated insights across asset classes to public and private market investors

Deliver differentiated insights across asset classes to public and private market investors

We remain committed to ensuring that the modern investor is empowered with new data, research, and analytics.

value.why_notable: Recurring, unusually explicit statement of Morningstar's no-guidance philosophy, framing management incentives directly.

notable_language.quote: We do not make public financial forecasts for our business because we want to avoid creating any incentives for our management team to make speculative statements about our financial results that could influence our stock price or take actions that help us meet short-term forecasts, but may not build long-term shareholder value.

value.why_notable: Direct admission of wage inflation and employee turnover pressure affecting the company, new emphasis relative to prior pandemic disclosure.

notable_language.quote: Certain long-term effects of the efforts of monetary authorities and governments to ameliorate the impacts of the pandemic are potentially starting to become evident, including both price and wage inflation as well as the competition for workers. We have noted these effects in our business related to the mobility of employees between jobs and the wage levels needed to hire or retain employees.

value.why_notable: Hedged COVID framing paired with an explicit claim of no significant revenue impact — a softening from earlier pandemic uncertainty language.

notable_language.quote: The threat of new variants of the virus and concerns over the adoption and efficacy of mitigants, such as vaccines and other treatments, continue to affect historical commercial and work patterns, although not with any significant impact on any of our sources of revenue during 2021.

value.why_notable: Acknowledges client losses in Investment Management, an admission embedded in otherwise positive growth commentary.

notable_language.quote: Investment Management revenue grew 6.1% in 2021, as stronger year-over-year inflows and market performance more than offset the negative impact of previously-disclosed client losses.

value.why_notable: Unusually direct admission that the company's own risk of inadvertent regulatory noncompliance has risen.

notable_language.quote: Given more intense regulatory scrutiny and the novelty of some of the issues presented, the possibilities for inadvertent noncompliance with regulation have increased.

value.why_notable: New-for-the-year topic; a plain statement of limited impact with a forward hedge on IT infrastructure.

notable_language.quote: Given the nature of our business, global supply chain disruptions have had little impact on the company, but could impact the availability of certain IT infrastructure over time.

value.why_notable: Explicit explanation of the reversal of the COVID-era weighting change back to the pre-pandemic mix, described as 'the optimal mix'.

notable_language.quote: We modified our annual incentive performance measure weightings for 2021 to 67% Adjusted Revenue and 33% Adjusted EBITDA. This represents the weighting which we believe is the optimal mix of performance measures for our annual incentive plan and is what we had in place in 2019. In 2020, we modified our weightings to 50% Adjusted Revenue and 50% Adjusted EBITDA in response to the COVID-19 pandemic and the uncertainty it caused.

value.why_notable: Justifies a doubling of upside leverage purely by reference to 'market practices'.

notable_language.quote: For our performance-based Market Stock Unit Program, starting with our November 2021 grant, we increased our maximum payout to 200% of target, which represents a change to align to market practices.

value.why_notable: Recurring philosophy statement reserving discretion while claiming formulaic alignment.

notable_language.quote: Does not use rigid formulas to determine executive compensation but nevertheless aims to tie annual cash incentive compensation closely to value creation, as measured by increases in Adjusted Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA or similar measures.

value.why_notable: Explains replacement of an objective revenue metric with a committee-determined discretionary kicker, still attributed to the pandemic in 2021.

notable_language.quote: The shift from a revenue kicker in 2019 to a performance kicker in 2020 and 2021 was made due to the uncertain market environment and uncertain three-year outlook due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

value.why_notable: Long-recurring rationale for the Executive Chairman's nominal pay, framed as his own request.

notable_language.quote: In consideration of his status as our principal shareholder, Joe believes that his compensation should be directly aligned with other shareholders and be realized primarily through appreciation in the long-term value of our common stock. At his request and supported by the Compensation Committee, he did not participate in our equity or cash-based incentive programs in 2021 and his salary has been $100,000 since 2000.

value.why_notable: Delayed COVID-era increases restored with an explicit below-median peer positioning claim as justification.

notable_language.quote: The Committee approved, for 2021, the original intended compensation increases from 2020. Starting January 1, 2021, his salary was $500,000 and target bonus was $1,000,000. In addition, the Committee increased Kunal’s target equity grant from $1,500,000 to $2,000,000. The Committee made these changes to improve the competitiveness of Kunal’s target total compensation. In total, Kunal’s target total compensation is below the median of the peer group.

value.why_notable: Pre-emptive framing of the year-over-year decline in reported CEO pay.

notable_language.quote: Although the 2021 Summary Compensation Table shows that Kunal’s total compensation decreased year-over-year, his 2020 compensation included a non-recurring restricted stock unit grant of $3,000,000 which will vest over five years, as disclosed in our 2021 proxy.

value.why_notable: Describes an extra equity award layered onto the bonus formula for above-target individual ratings.

notable_language.quote: In 2021, Morningstar rewarded its top performers (those whose individual performance adjustment was above 100%) with a restricted stock unit award that vests in two equal annual installments commencing on the first anniversary of the grant date.

value.why_notable: Unusually direct admission of a stock ownership compliance failure and a granted waiver.

notable_language.quote: Due to an administrative error, Gail Landis is not currently in compliance but has a plan is in place to achieve compliance no later than the second quarter of 2022. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee has reviewed the facts and granted Gail a waiver to the stock ownership requirements for this period of time.

value.why_notable: Uses the 97% say-on-pay result to justify making no changes.

notable_language.quote: Given the significant shareholder support, the Compensation Committee did not make any changes to the Company’s executive compensation program in response to the 2021 say on pay vote.

value.why_notable: Tightening of ownership requirements announced alongside the increase in MSU maximum payout.

notable_language.quote: Stock ownership is a cornerstone of our executive compensation program. In December 2021, we increased the holding requirement for total number of vested restricted stock units and vested market stock units from 25% to 33% for our NEOs.

value.topic: DBRS Morningstar strategic direction and investment plans in credit ratings
value.stated_position: Management said it is "confident in the increasing role DBRS Morningstar plays in the global markets," intends to "expand our corporate ratings footprint" and continue investing in global structured finance for traditional and non-traditional assets, framing these investments as "a stable path towards adjacent growth in the ratings delivery and fixed income data markets."

investor_qa.quote: Overall, we are confident in the increasing role DBRS Morningstar plays in the global markets. We intend to expand our corporate ratings footprint and will continue to invest in the global structured finance markets related to both traditional and non-traditional assets. While beneficial in its own right, these investments also provide a stable path towards adjacent growth in the ratings delivery and fixed income data markets.

value.topic: DBRS Morningstar plans to drive market share against the legacy rating agencies
value.stated_position: In Canada management claims "market-leading positions" driven by "local expertise, existing market presence, and extensive track record"; beyond Canada it acknowledges "the three large legacy credit ratings agencies enjoy safeguards against new entrants," and targets "smaller, private, or transactional issues," European share gains as an "eligible credit rating agency," and the U.S. corporate middle market leveraging "our 45-year experience in assessing complex corporates, our more-granular pricing model, and our local expertise."

investor_qa.quote: Beyond Canada, the three large legacy credit ratings agencies enjoy safeguards against new entrants in existing market segments, especially when bond issues are larger, public, and recurring. However, when the market seeks ratings on smaller, private, or transactional issues, all registered credit ratings agencies have the opportunity to compete. These are the focus areas where DBRS Morningstar has been highly successful to date in expanding its footprint and where we will continue to further accelerate our market presence.

value.topic: Whether the SEC investigation will change the credit ratings business
value.stated_position: Management stated it does not believe the SEC complaint against Morningstar's former credit ratings organization will cause any material disruptions or changes to current credit ratings strategy or operations.

investor_qa.quote: At this time, we do not believe the SEC complaint against Morningstar’s former credit ratings organization will cause any material disruptions or changes to our current credit ratings strategy or operations.

value.topic: Free cash flow priorities and capital allocation
value.stated_position: "We continue to take a balanced approach to capital allocation. Our primary emphasis is supporting organic growth; however, we will continue to pursue acquisitions opportunistically." Dividends have had fairly consistent growth rates and payout ratios since 2010; share repurchases are evaluated like any investment and are not "programmatic."

investor_qa.quote: We continue to take a balanced approach to capital allocation. Our primary emphasis is supporting organic growth; however, we will continue to pursue acquisitions opportunistically. Since declaring our first dividend in 2010, we have maintained fairly consistent dividend growth rates and payout ratios. We evaluate share repurchases much like we would any investment, prioritizing available capital against the potential return of the investment, and do not utilize a “programmatic” approach.

investor_qa.quote: While we are focused on effectively integrating our recent acquisitions into Morningstar, our ongoing strategy includes identifying opportunities that accelerate our ability to empower investor success while creating value for the business and investors. We currently have many in-flight and planned initiatives to grow the business organically, but we are always monitoring the landscape for interesting opportunities that could add to or strengthen our capabilities.

value.topic: In-house versus third-party management within Managed Portfolios

investor_qa.quote: Currently, we do not offer third-party model portfolio providers (or “strategists”) within Managed Portfolios. We manage the asset allocation and underlying investment vehicle targets of these portfolios.

investor_qa.quote: It is true, on the other hand, that growth in assets under management have lagged our most recent combined market estimate growth rate of over 20% in both Workplace Solutions and Investment Management. value.topic: Founder Joe Mansueto's ownership succession

investor_qa.quote: As of December 31, 2020, we estimate that approximately 33% of our license-based revenues come from advisors, 25% from asset managers, and 22% from private market investors, with the remainder split amongst redistributors, retail investors, buyside investors, and the retirement market. value.topic: PitchBook client mix shift toward Companies segment

investor_qa.quote: Since 2016, the Company client segment has exhibited the greatest expansion, and now represents about 30% of our total client count. Companies have also been our fastest growing segment in the past 18 months and represents an extension of PitchBook’s customer profile.

value.topic: PitchBook total addressable market sizing and methodology

investor_qa.quote: We estimate that our total addressable market is $3.5 billion globally, an increase of approximately 52.2% since the $2.3 billion figure we shared at the 2020 Annual Meeting.

value.topic: PitchBook long-term margin potential

value.topic: PitchBook competitive position versus S&P Capital IQ
value.stated_position: Management observes Capital IQ "continues to pursue a partnership or acquisition strategy to build its private market data sets" and states "We believe PitchBook holds a competitive advantage in the market through our primary and secondary research processes and data coverage of areas important to our customers," citing a commissioned blind brand study in which PitchBook earned 33% of votes versus 7% for S&P Capital IQ.

investor_qa.quote: We believe PitchBook holds a competitive advantage in the market through our primary and secondary research processes and data coverage of areas important to our customers.

value.topic: Strategy for monetizing DBRS Morningstar credit data
value.stated_position: Management agrees credit data is a growth opportunity with four dimensions — credit ratings data (RatingsNow), credit research, fixed income reference data (where "DBRS Morningstar does not offer a product in this area at present"), and normalized fixed-income credit data — and states the intent to replace third-party financial metrics with internal data across DBRS Morningstar, Morningstar and PitchBook.

value.topic: DBRS Morningstar EMEA growth plans

investor_qa.quote: Our immediate focus is on maintaining our very good coverage in the European structured markets (outside the CLO space) while building our footprint in fundamental ratings. With our existing ratings coverage of sovereigns and leading banks, our specific objective is to build the demand for corporate ratings used for private placements and middle market lending.

value.topic: DBRS Morningstar relative profitability by region and margin ambition
value.stated_position: Management says it feels comfortable with profitability in "leading" segments even though overall revenue is of modest size relative to larger competitors; Canadian margins benefit from more fundamental ratings and recurring revenue, while US and Europe core profitability is lower given transaction-based structured finance and ongoing investment. investor_qa.quote: Our goal, over time, is to turn more of our “established” market segments into “leading” segments, which we believe will favorably impact our margin profile.

investor_qa.quote: Our growth strategy for Morningstar’s ESG business encompasses three main avenues. The first is growing Sustainalytics’ leadership position in ESG-related ratings, research, and data, the second is expanding Sustainalytics’ position in sustainable finance, and the third is integrating Sustainalytics’ IP into Morningstar’s portfolio of offerings.

value.topic: ESG addressable market sizing

"We continue to refine our understanding of that addressable market."

investor_qa.quote: Furthermore, most published estimates of the ESG market size understandably focus on the institutional investor market, which we believe is too limited a focus. Sustainalytics and Morningstar aim to make ESG investing accessible to all investors, not just professional investors.

value.topic: Integration of Sustainalytics onto Morningstar infrastructure
value.stated_position: Management describes leveraging Morningstar technology at the corporate systems, technology operations, and product technology levels, with a "clear roadmap to complete this adoption by end of 2021," and says Morningstar's platforms have wide distribution to retail wealth "which is where we intend to increasingly surface and integrate Sustainalytics' ESG research and data."

investor_qa.quote: From a customer reach standpoint, Morningstar’s platforms have wide distribution capability to the retail wealth customer segment, which is where we intend to increasingly surface and integrate Sustainalytics’ ESG research and data.

value.topic: Sustainalytics differentiation versus MSCI

investor_qa.quote: The primary differentiator between Sustainalytics and MSCI is that the methodology underpinning Sustainalytics’ ESG Risk Rating takes an absolute approach to highlighting risk, which allows investors to evaluate companies across sectors and geographies using consistent standards.

value.topic: Sustainalytics position in green/sustainable bond second party opinions and overlap with DBRS
value.stated_position: Management cites Environmental Finance recognizing Sustainalytics as "the leading external reviewer of green/social/sustainability bonds with 36.5% market share," nearly equal to the next four competitors combined, and states "The products of Sustainalytics and DBRS Morningstar do not overlap in these efforts" — they are "complementary products for issuers."

investor_qa.quote: The products of Sustainalytics and DBRS Morningstar do not overlap in these efforts, as the focus and meaning of a credit rating assigned by DBRS Morningstar differs from the second party opinion by Sustainalytics. We consider these complementary products for issuers.

value.topic: ESG partnerships versus acquisitions

investor_qa.quote: To that point, we look at partnership and acquisition strategies separately. While we do not have an acquisition “wish list”, Morningstar always surveys the landscape for value-creating acquisition opportunities.

investor_qa.quote: Regulatory datasets, including those used to satisfy MiFID II requirements, have made the most meaningful contribution to Morningstar Data’s revenue growth over the past three years. ESG-related datasets have been the second strongest driver of revenue growth,

value.topic: Morningstar Direct license renewal pressure and product transition

investor_qa.quote: At Morningstar Direct, even though we’ve seen consistency in new customer acquisition rates in recent years, we’ve experienced some pressure on license renewals as we work through evolving our legacy desktop-based product toward a flexible framework that enables the delivery of modern web components to both the desktop and web-versions of Direct.

value.topic: Reason for moving Morningstar Direct to the cloud
value.stated_position: "We decided to evolve the Morningstar Direct framework to the cloud to provide us and our clients with increased flexibility," enabling more frequent and efficient enhancements and client access "anytime, anywhere."

investor_qa.quote: We decided to evolve the Morningstar Direct framework to the cloud to provide us and our clients with increased flexibility. Morningstar would be able to deliver enhancements to the products on a more frequent, more efficient basis, while our clients would be able to access our content anytime, anywhere.

value.topic: Distribution-agnostic strategy and competition with FactSet and Bloomberg
value.stated_position: "Morningstar has always taken the approach that the data, research, ratings and other content that we provide investors can and should be consumed however our clients want to consume it." FactSet and Bloomberg are competitors but also redistribute Morningstar data and pay to use it; "We have the ability to extract value from our offerings no matter the distribution channel."

investor_qa.quote: Factset and Bloomberg are indeed competitors, but they also redistribute some of our proprietary data to their clients and pay us to use it in their products. We have the ability to extract value from our offerings no matter the distribution channel, which underscores the need we ultimately fill in the value chain.

value.topic: Client stickiness and churn causes in Data and Direct
value.stated_position: Management says its IP is embedded in client workflows, investment policies and compliance regimens, and "we believe that losing access to our IP is as much a source of the stickiness as the technical consequences of switching." "Churn in our core client base is more frequently due to consolidation or restructuring at our clients' firms and less so because of competitive dynamics."

investor_qa.quote: Churn in our core client base is more frequently due to consolidation or restructuring at our clients’ firms and less so because of competitive dynamics, although that does happen from time to time. Generally speaking, however, the stickiness of our business model does have a protective effect against competition.

value.topic: Key growth areas and investing "ahead of the curve"
value.stated_position: Management identifies "key growth areas" as PitchBook, DBRS Morningstar, Morningstar Data, Morningstar Direct, Investment Management, and Workplace Solutions, representing "nearly 70% of our revenue," with Indexes and Sustainalytics named as other fast-growing areas of heavy investment, and an intent to invest in ESG-enabled solutions across the portfolio.

investor_qa.quote: For some time, we’ve referred to our “key growth areas” as products that we believe have the potential to generate outsized growth, which includes PitchBook, DBRS Morningstar, Morningstar Data, Morningstar Direct, Investment Management, and Workplace Solutions. We’re fortunate that these product areas represent nearly 70% of our revenue

value.topic: Expected five-year business mix and margin profile
value.stated_position: "We've centered our efforts on continuing to support the development of differentiated products and solutions, investing for scale in multiple areas of our business, and expanding our leadership position in ESG across the portfolio." Management expects license-based areas to remain the largest revenue component for the foreseeable future and does not expect mix shift to be the primary driver of margin change; rather margins should improve "as we scale and benefit from operating leverage."

investor_qa.quote: We have attractive growth opportunities across our portfolio but would expect our licensed based areas to continue to be the largest component of our revenue for the foreseeable future. Furthermore, we do not expect the primary driver of change in our margin profile to come from mix shift; rather, we’d expect to see our margins improve over time as we scale and benefit from operating leverage.

value.topic: M&A priorities and process
value.stated_position: "While we don't comment on our plans for future M&A, in the past we have made acquisitions to enhance our capabilities, particularly from a technology perspective, or to support growth in areas of the business where we see outsized potential." DBRS is cited as improving scale in credit ratings, Sustainalytics as supporting ESG product development, and AdviserLogic and PlanPlus as growing financial planning. Decisions weigh financial returns and strategic and cultural fit, and "our focus on organic growth means that we don't prioritize acquisitions for the sake of activity."

investor_qa.quote: We have an established process to identify, evaluate, and prioritize acquisition opportunities. Our decisions are based on many factors with financial returns, and strategic and cultural fit being critical. Importantly, our focus on organic growth means that we don’t prioritize acquisitions for the sake of activity.

value.topic: Competitive landscape and churn drivers for Morningstar Data and Direct
value.stated_position: Management said the primary driver of churn is client consolidation/restructuring, not competitive losses, and that it has "a long, successful history of competing with various data and platform providers" and typically wins and retains clients "based on the unique attributes of the products and services we provide."

investor_qa.quote: We believe that the primary driver of churn in these product areas is client consolidation/ restructuring. We have a long, successful history of competing with various data and platform providers and typically win and retain clients based on the unique attributes of the products and services we provide.

value.topic: Morningstar Data's competitive strengths
value.stated_position: Management characterizes Morningstar Data's advantage as proprietary datasets, like managed fund data, that competitors have historically been unable to replicate at similar breadth and depth, conceding local competitors like Financial Express can occasionally offer a competitive dataset for a particular country.

investor_qa.quote: We believe that Morningstar Data’s competitive strengths lie in its proprietary datasets, like managed fund data, that competitors have historically been unable to replicate at a similar breadth and depth. Occasionally, companies like Financial Express can offer a competitive dataset for a particular country or geographical area due to their local presences, but we tend to retain clients that rely on the more comprehensive offering that we provide.

value.topic: What growth in Morningstar Direct depends on
value.stated_position: Management states that growth ultimately hinges on the ability to build new datasets and deliver efficiencies in clients' workflows, with client retention driven by proprietary datasets and ease of incorporating clients' own data.

investor_qa.quote: Ultimately, growth in Morningstar Direct hinges on our ability to build new datasets and deliver efficiencies in our clients’ workflows. Clients tend to stay with us because of the proprietary datasets they consume through the platform, as well as the ease of incorporating their own proprietary data sets into our custom calculations and templates.

value.topic: ESG demand and integration of Sustainalytics into Morningstar Direct
value.stated_position: Management reports growing client demand for ESG-related datasets, particularly in Europe due to the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation, and says it has continued to pull Sustainalytics functionality into Morningstar Direct, most recently company-level ESG Risk Ratings.

investor_qa.quote: Recently, we’ve seen growing demand from clients for ESG-related datasets, which give Morningstar Direct users specific information regarding a fund’s sustainability factors. This functionality has particularly resonated in Europe due to the recently enacted Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation, but we have also seen interest rise in other markets. We’ve also continued to pull functionality from Sustainalytics into Morningstar Direct, most recently displaying company-level ESG Risk Ratings next to companies that are covered by a Sustainalytics analyst.

value.topic: Impact of the shift from active to passive management
value.stated_position: Management argues assets under active management are not in decline "despite the headlines" and that as long as actively-managed assets continue to show growth, active managers will continue to rely on Morningstar's services; it declines to give an apples-to-apples revenue comparison because passive AUM growth "does not represent a perfect negative correlation with revenue on the active management side."

investor_qa.quote: First, while we agree that passive management is a clear source of growth in the market, our data suggests that assets under active management are not in decline despite the headlines.

value.topic: Automation versus passive investing as a threat to seat growth
value.stated_position: Management suspects automation across financial services has a greater impact on platform seat growth than passive investing, and says that even if clients reduce Direct seats, Morningstar often picks up business from the same client through data licenses or redistribution rights.

investor_qa.quote: If anything, we suspect that the rise of automation across the financial services industry has a greater impact on platform seat growth than passive investing; however, even if clients reduce seats of Direct due to automating parts of their business, we often pick up business from the same client through Morningstar Data by offering them data licenses or redistribution rights.

value.topic: Product offerings aimed at passive investors
value.stated_position: Management says it has added solutions specifically meeting the needs of passive investors, such as Morningstar Indexes, private equity and ESG data and analytics, and positions itself as agnostic: "We are here to serve our clients' needs no matter what method of investing is in favor."

investor_qa.quote: Moreover, we’ve added solutions across our product offerings that specifically meet the needs of passive investors, such as Morningstar Indexes, which has shown healthy levels of growth, as well as private equity and ESG data and analytics. We are here to serve our clients’ needs no matter what method of investing is in favor.

value.topic: Drivers of asset-based revenue growth and competitive position in Morningstar Indexes
value.stated_position: Management said market performance "was not the sole contributor" to asset-based revenue, pointing to AUM growth in Workplace Solutions "aided by growth in new plans and participants, and new funds being added to existing plans," "strengthening flows in Managed Portfolios within Investment Management and momentum in Morningstar Indexes as clients continue to seek alternative index providers."

investor_qa.quote: Since last year, AUM growth in Workplace Solutions has also been aided by growth in new plans and participants, and new funds being added to existing plans. We’ve also experienced strengthening flows in Managed Portfolios within Investment Management and momentum in Morningstar Indexes as clients continue to seek alternative index providers.

value.topic: Reliance on third-party distributors/redistributors for data products
value.stated_position: "We do not consider ourselves reliant on third-party distribution. In aggregate, redistributors generate a relatively small portion of our consolidated revenue." Management says it aims to deliver its IP wherever clients work, and believes it has "struck the right balance" between direct sales and redistributors.

investor_qa.quote: Overall, we believe we have struck the right balance between selling directly to investors and using redistributors to reach investors we wouldn’t ordinarily reach on our own while capturing the appropriate value.

value.topic: Pricing strategy for ESG data — basic vs. premium
value.stated_position: Basic ESG data and insights are "value-added enhancements within our software platforms" included in the software license and "essentially baked into our year-over-year price increases, allowing us to negotiate from a point of strength," while more granular ESG data sets are sold as add-ons via entitlements.

investor_qa.quote: This data set is included in our software license and is essentially baked into our year-over-year price increases, allowing us to negotiate from a point of strength. More granular ESG data sets are sold as add-ons, accessed through an entitlement on our platforms.

value.topic: Sustainalytics' competitive advantages and vision
value.stated_position: Key differentiator is the ability to work with investors across the whole investment value chain, plus a differentiated research methodology underpinning the ESG Risk Rating capturing managed and unmanaged risk, and a large responsive customer service organization. Larger competitors can bundle ESG as an add-on; being part of Morningstar gives more bundling opportunities to extend reach, particularly in retail wealth.

investor_qa.quote: With Sustainalytics now a part of the larger Morningstar organization, we have more opportunities to bundle complementary offerings, and believe that this strategy can ultimately help Sustainalytics extend its reach to new customers, particularly in retail wealth.

value.topic: Regulation as a barrier to entry in indexes and ESG ratings
value.stated_position: Management argues benchmark regulation raises barriers to entry, benefiting existing index providers and making self-indexing less economically attractive; owning the underlying ESG data (Sustainalytics) plus portfolio calculation expertise gives Morningstar "a significant advantage." It views emerging ESG regulation as "a floor, rather than ceiling" and cites the Moorgate Benchmarks acquisition as bolstering its position as a registered benchmark administrator in the UK and EU.

investor_qa.quote: We believe that the increased regulatory and administrator burden, and the significant financial sanctions that apply under the BMRs, mean self-indexing is a less attractive option economically, benefiting existing index providers such as Morningstar.

value.topic: Managing conflicts of interest in independent research
value.stated_position: "Morningstar has a long history of managing conflicts related to running a business based on independent research." It applies the same standards to ESG research as to mutual fund ratings, and its Code of Ethics prohibits salespeople from contacting mutual fund and equity analysts.

investor_qa.quote: Our Morningstar Code of Ethics specifically prohibits salespeople from contacting mutual fund and equity analysts. Our practices are thoroughly documented in our policies and procedures, which are reviewed by compliance as well as applicable regulatory authorities.

value.topic: Biggest obstacle to faster PitchBook growth
value.stated_position: Talent is the common denominator; "perhaps the biggest near-term challenge is to hire quickly enough at the quality we expect to meet the demand for our solutions." Management intends to continue to invest heavily in PitchBook's go-to-market and product development strategy.

investor_qa.quote: At PitchBook, and across Morningstar, perhaps the biggest near-term challenge is to hire quickly enough at the quality we expect to meet the demand for our solutions.

value.topic: How the board and management prioritise projects and allocate capital
value.stated_position: Management names the areas it has "called out" as best long-run growth opportunities — Morningstar Data, Morningstar Direct, DBRS Morningstar, PitchBook, Investment Management, Workplace, and Indexes — with ESG now another key area of focus and investment. Uses the OKR framework Kunal described in his annual shareholder letter; management and Board attend an annual off-site strategy meeting; investment philosophy characterized as "long-term oriented in nature."

investor_qa.quote: These include Morningstar Data, Morningstar Direct, DBRS Morningstar, PitchBook, Investment Management, Workplace, and Indexes. With the addition of Sustainalytics, ESG is another key area of focus and investment.

value.topic: Cost growth versus revenue growth and level of investment spend
value.stated_position: "Our goal over the long-term is to grow revenue in excess of expense growth and expand our adjusted operating margin," with the belief the opportunity set is significant and that the company is "moving with speed to increase our leadership position in areas such as ESG."

investor_qa.quote: Our belief remains that our opportunity set is significant, and we are moving with speed to increase our leadership position in areas such as ESG. Our goal over the long-term is to grow revenue in excess of expense growth and expand our adjusted operating margin.

value.topic: Profitability by division and organizational structure

segments_basis.basis: product or business areas described in Item 1 — this filing does not disclose reportable segments, so these are NOT segments and must not be compared with a year that does

investor_qa_basis.basis: management's written answers to questions submitted by investors, published roughly monthly. Same verification as every other fact — whole-document boundaries and a checked quote — but a different kind of evidence from a 10-K or proxy statement: unaudited, unprompted by any disclosure requirement, and responsive to whatever was asked. Corroborating; not a substitute for a filed disclosure.

ids.basis: content hash of the claim, its evidence and its source — see `fact_id` in src/equity_research/ledger_schema.py. Confidence and the verification result are NOT hashed, so re-verifying a fact does not renumber it. Cross-year uniqueness is enforced fatally at build time by `audit_ids`.

document_window.basis: filing dates of the documents this year's facts are actually drawn from — NOT the fiscal window in inventory.json, which bounds the fiscal years in scope. Documents reporting on a fiscal year are filed after it ends, so this range extends past window_end_date by construction. Any accession listed above additionally belongs to a fiscal year outside the window and is used deliberately: an annual-meeting vote held in May of year N decides on year N-1.

corrections.basis: config/corrections.toml — human corrections to model-extracted values that the cited filing contradicts, each carrying the filing text that establishes it. data/ledger/facts/ is never edited: the record of what the model returned has to stay as it was.
